code_only_features.feature_name: reassuring prefix/suffix added to subject prompts during calm-data generation
code_only_features.evidence: src/calm_data.py:51-57 `_augment_user` prepends REASSURING_PREFIX (turn 1) and appends REASSURING_SUFFIX (follow-ups) to the user message, and is actually called in generate_conversations at src/calm_data.py:88 (`user_msg = _augment_user(turn, base, reassure)`) before model.generate, so when reassure=True the subject genuinely receives softening text in those conversations. NOTE: this only runs in the calm-data *training-data* generation path (reassure=True), NOT in the main distress-elicitation rollout (src/rollouts.py) or petri loop, both of which deliver only rejections/criticism with no reassurance and no early stop; the scaffolding is also stripped from the stored dataset (src/calm_data.py:99). The main experiment loop (rollouts.run_rollout) runs the full cond.n_turns with the per-turn frustration score recorded but never read to break/cap, and HIGH_FRUSTRATION_THRESHOLD / score>=7 are used only for post-hoc analysis and sample selection (analysis.py:62, run_prefilling.py:37), so there is no hard_stop, debrief, consent, or distress-triggered protective_monitoring anywhere.
code_only_features.justification_quote: To generate calm responses from Gemma-3-27B-Instruct we sample responses to impossible numeric questions with a reassuring *prefix* ... (calm_data module docstring) -- purpose is finetuning-data generation, not in-experiment subject protection; the reassuring text is generation scaffolding that is then stripped (src/calm_data.py:99 comment: 'Store the *stripped* (unreassured) user message so the dataset doesn't carry the supportive scaffolding')
